I have a queen anne canopy bed. The foundations were aged and creaky. In doing some research on replacing them, I realized that in this style of bed the foundations or box (no)spring mattress weren't explicitly required as long as you had a solid platform from...something. I was looking at spending 400 dollars for new foundations to fit this massive thing. I wasn't happy at all with the last ones because they made my mattress feel like quicksand.

Instead of buying, I made my own foundations outta yellow pine and reinforced my bed to ensure it stays solid for another hundred years. The mattress feels better. The bed looks better as more of the ornate carvings are visible on the headboard. The bed is completely silent when you move around in it. I don't need a ladder to get into it anymore and I saved 320 bucks using stuff I already had around the house.

If you're sleeping on a metal frame, you could be doing so much better. There's some really fantastic and easy bed builds that you can do for roughly the cost of your mattress and foundation. Stuff will look great and last for eternity. Google DIY platform beds.

Story time: I pick up a hitchhiker and it turns out to be someone super important

I was in my hometown for a week for my father's birthday, and I was checking the Facebook page of a Music Festival I was going to which was 7 hours away. On this page, there was this woman who was looking for a ride to the venue, and she happened to be in my hometown and wanted to be back at the same time I did. My girlfriend and I were somewhat skeptical about it at first. We saw that she was also needing a ticket to get in, which made us even more skeptical because she's kinda broke. Looking at her pictures, she looked like the stereotypical, run-of-the-mill hippie. Upon more Facebook stalking, we also see that she has a kid, so we were somewhat relieved (people who have kids and post about them on Facebook usually aren't out to fuck you over).

We go to pick her up, and she wants to bring A LOT of stuff, and we end up leaving about an hour later than we had planned on originally, but nevertheless were on the road finally. As we got to talking, it turns out she was a well-respected member of one of the Grateful Dead families and an old-school raver from the 1990s-2000s. And she happened to be a felon for selling MDMA and LSD in bulk. Regardless of that, I still wasn't too off-put. We were still trying to get a feel for each other. The whole ride up there, she was namedropping all sorts of names of people we had never heard of and telling all sorts of crazy stories, and I was thinking she was just blowing smoke and talking herself up.

When we finally get to the venue, she starts talking to people and the people at the front gate actually know her, which was kind of a surprise. Turns out, all of those stories she told were absolutely 100% true. She really is in one of The Grateful Dead families - rings, pins, and everything. We find our campsite and almost immediately, she finds my girlfriend and I a dealer with a gram of MDMA at friend/family prices (not average customer prices, which were much more). She was going to find for us a person with LSD, but we already had our own, and that never really came through. She was kind of hard to find sometimes, and was constantly going from one place to another.

Also, at the festival, around noon on Saturday, my girlfriend and I were by the river hanging out and taking a quick dip to cool off when a couple came down and let their kid play around. Turned out the 'couple' were actually just friends, but dated once upon a time. The kid was 5 years old, and had A TON of energy and was somewhat rebellious. I was looking at rocks, and the guy was too, and it turned out he was an unemployed geologist (like me) and also an Eagle Scout (like me). He was also on an adderall prescription (like me), and his Eagle Scout project was almost identical to mine (fixing a playground sandbox). FREAKING CRAZY COINCIDENCE. He even dressed like me - cargo shorts, nondescript generic t-shirt, beard with a few days growth, same haircut. They were a great 'couple,' but it's just weird that they're not together but still occasionally have sex, are both raising that kid (it's not his), but are officially 'just friends.'

I didn't end up sleeping Saturday night due to a combination of various wacky molecules and way-cool thoughts, and Sunday morning, it rained as we were packing up getting ready to go. It took us forever to find the person we gave a ride there, and left about an hour later than we had wanted to.

The ride there and back was done in two parts. On the way up, my girlfriend and I took my car to her car, and during that drive to her car, my window kinda fucked up. It had this problem before, where the tracks fuck up, and the window falls into the door. Unfortunately, the woman we were giving the ride to was sitting there, and so for a portion of the drive there AND the entire drive home, the window was constantly down. When we got back to my car, my girlfriend went back to where she's currently living because she had work this morning; the hitchhiker and I drove home. She was tripping the whole ride back, but was never short of words or conversation - she talked about her husband, her daughter, what God means to her, how to raise kids, etc.

Now, I am just relaxing. It was a great weekend overall. Would do it all again.

The author says stuff like:

We will only have mitigated it and prettified it. We will have found relief from the crisis, but not a resolution of it.

What's wrong with mitigating a crisis? The deal reduces the ability of Iran to get nuclear weapons. Realistically, that's all that can be done. Even if they gave up all their nuclear infrastructure that just reduces their ability, not eliminates it, it can be rebuilt.

The author also seems to have a pretty low view of the Iranian regime. Is that really justified? The regime is theocratic, but Iran is certainly more democratic than, say, Saudi Arabia. If Iran has enmity towards the US, is that not justified by history?
